Subject: SLA template: monthly credit cap and exclusions — quick ask

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and procurement reviewed the draft SLA and we have two asks before we can proceed to signature:

1) Monthly credit cap — the draft lists a vendor-friendly cap that compresses remedy for high-availability customers. For our use case (real-time inference in financial alerts) we need a higher monthly credit cap or an exception bucket for severity impacts.
2) Exclusions and maintenance carve-outs — we need clearer language for planned maintenance windows that might run longer during cross-region failovers; the current template's maintenance carve-outs could be interpreted too broadly.

Can you share an alternative cap schedule and a short suggested carve-out clause (1 paragraph) that your legal is comfortable with? We need to present something to our CFO by EOD Thursday.

Appreciate the help —
Ken

Ken —

Thanks for the clear asks and the timeline. I've looped Ben (sales lead on the account) and Marissa (legal ops/product counsel) in this thread. High level, we can offer two pragmatic paths:

Option A (standard enterprise compromise)
- Monthly remedy cap = 50% of one month’s committed spend (higher than the standard 30% in our public template).
- Severity bands remain as drafted; we can widen the monthly cap specifically for availability incidents that cause % of requests to fail > 15% for a 24h window.

Option B (guardrail + escrow)
- Monthly remedy cap = 100% of one month’s committed spend but limited to a combined 3-month rolling window per 12-month period.
- Add an operational exclusion list limited to: (i) customer misconfiguration; (ii) force majeure; (iii) customer-directed failover/testing. Cross-region failovers for our initiated maintenance would not be excluded.

Attached is a redline of the SLA template (redwood-sla-template-v2.pdf) and a quick credit matrix (service-credit-matrix.xlsx) showing the two options side-by-side. Marissa — can you take a pass on tightening the maintenance carve-out language (one paragraph our legal can accept)?

If either option looks workable for NorthBay, we can draft a short amendment and route it through DocuSign today.

Best,

Ken / Ben / Priya —

Quick draft paragraph to address NorthBay's maintenance carve-out concern (keeps vendor protections but closes the broad wording):

"Planned Maintenance and Cross-Region Operations: Redwood will provide at least 72 hours’ notice for planned maintenance expected to materially affect availability. Planned maintenance does not include emergency remediation or capacity-related failovers initiated by either party to preserve service continuity. Maintenance windows that result from Redwood-initiated cross-region migrations performed as part of an agreed outage remediation plan are subject to prior customer notification and shall not be considered an exclusion for monthly remedy calculations unless the customer has expressly directed the migration.

This language aims to prevent broad exclusions that could remove remedies for customer-impacting cross-region work; it preserves the ability to schedule necessary maintenance while protecting NorthBay from losing remedy rights for Redwood-initiated failovers.

On credits: my recommended compromise is Option A (50% cap) for now; Option B is viable but requires C-suite sign-off due to the higher exposure. If we take Option B we suggest a rolling-window guardrail and a monthly cap floor so credits can't exceed monthly spend more than once per quarter.

Ben — can you confirm commercial comfort with Option A for NB-4521? If yes, I'll prepare the amendment language and a short cover memo for procurement.

—Marissa

Ken —

Thanks for surfacing this. Commercially we can accept Option A (50% monthly cap) as a standard for NorthBay given the mission-critical nature of your workloads. We'll include the maintenance carve-out paragraph Marissa drafted and add the following clarifying bullets to the amendment: 

- "Remedy cap applicability: Credits for availability incidents are calculated against the monthly committed spend for the impacted product line. Credits are cumulative across severity bands but capped at 50% monthly spend for any single month.
- Operational carve-outs: Customer-directed actions, demonstrable misconfigurations, and force majeure remain exclusions. Redwood-initiated cross-region migrations performed as emergency remediation are not exclusions unless expressly requested by the customer.
- Escalation & monitoring: For incidents that may approach the monthly cap, Redwood will provide weekly account-level incident summaries and an optional on-call war room for joint triage.

If that aligns, Priya will circulate the amendment + redline for e-signature and we can target DocuSign by EOD Friday. Ken — please confirm and I'll proceed.
